citation.title: Mesh diagram cephalometric norms for Americans of African descent
citation.journal: American Journal of Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 13 differences; logs/task9b2-compare-baileytaylor1998.log). Every value re-read from the page images (PDF p. 4 = p. 221, Table V; PDF p. 5 = p. 222, Table VI). Decisions: (1) six means a = Table V, b = Table VI (SNA 86.0/86.08, SNB 80.3/80.48, ANB 5.7/5.6, UI-NA 22.0/22.35, UI-SN 108.6/108.68, LI-MP 101.1/100.92) -> Table VI, the other table's value in each note (merge notes P25: Table VI where both print the row, Table V only where VI lacks it; interincisal 118.2 is Table V only). (2) LI-MP -> #59 a 'same', b 'close' -> same: p. 223 (PDF p. 6; the merge notes said p. 222, the page shows 223) says the authors drew the mandibular plane as Steiner does, from Go to gnathion. (3) Source wording a/b differ (prose). Values found by one extractor only: none (both 9 rows). SN-MP 31.84 and overbite 2.51 are Table VI only and were checked on p. 222. n not entered per row: the tables print none (groups 1 + 2 = 18 + 23 = 41 children aged 8-12, p. 219). Selection class-I-balanced: Class I skeletal and molar, balanced profile by consensus of at least three of four examiners, untreated (p. 219). headPosition unknown (b; a said NHP, but natural head position was used only to orient the mesh tracings, p. 220). Scale not-stated (no magnification statement; hand traced with a millimetre ruler, p. 219).

caveats: No SD anywhere: the paper says it calculated means, SDs and p values (p. 220) but prints only means. Every entry is a mean with no SD of its own; the app borrows an SD from the closest matching paper and says so.
Only the 8-12 y group (boys and girls together, 'Group I (1995)') of Tables V and VI has catalogue values; the 13-20 y groups and the by-sex groups have no table of catalogue measurements.

Sample size: the study measured 71 children and adolescents (29 F, 42 M, 8-20 y, p. 219); every entry here stands on the 8-12 y groups 1 and 2 (18 girls + 23 boys = 41, p. 219), so the set's n is 41 (fix round 1).

Tables V and VI print slightly different values for the same 8-12 y group (e.g. SNA 86.0 vs 86.08); the paper does not say why (p. 220 says only that in some cases ages were adjusted so the groups could be compared). Table VI used where it has the row (two decimals), Table V for the interincisal angle.

Not in the catalogue: S-N and N-ANS by group (Table IV, p. 221: girls 8-12 68.7 / 48.5; boys 8-12 72.2 / 51.8; females 13-20 70.2 / 51.7; males 13-20 75.7 / 55.5 mm, means only); SN to extracranial vertical 82.7° (p. 221).
The mesh diagrams (Figs. 3-6) are drawings: no landmark coordinates are printed. Nothing to enter.
The comparison columns (Taylor & Hitchcock's whites, Alexander's 1978 African-Americans) are other samples and are not entered.
Film scale: the paper says nothing about radiographic enlargement or its correction (only angles and one mm value, overbite, are entered).

entries.definitionNote: The paper defines overbite only as the upper/lower incisor overlap (Table III); the reference line (this app's: at right angles to the occlusal plane through the molars and incisors) is not stated.
